slides: Welcome back, and now more patterns. Remember, in pattern questions we don't use school formulas. We write it out, term by term, and a little psychometric thinking can make it shorter.

slides.say: Some patterns repeat in a cycle. Then one remainder trick saves us the whole list.

The days of the week repeat every seven days. Today is Tuesday. What day is it in thirty days? Thirty is four full weeks, twenty-eight days, plus two. Four full weeks bring us back to Tuesday. Two more days, and it's Thursday.

Why does it work? A full cycle always brings us back to where we started. So only the part after the full cycles matters, and that's the remainder. Let's see one more example. Today is Sunday. What day is it in fifteen days? Fifteen is fourteen plus one. Two full weeks, and one more day, so it's Monday.
Last digits of powers repeat too. What's the last digit of three to the power of twenty-two? Let's write the first few powers. Three, nine, twenty-seven, eighty-one, and then two hundred forty-three.

The last digits are three, nine, seven, one, and then three again. Why does it repeat? The next last digit comes only from the last digit times three. After one, we get three again, so the cycle starts over. It's a cycle of four.
Twenty-two is five full cycles, twenty, plus two. So we land on the second digit of the cycle, nine.
Careful when the remainder is zero. Then it's not the first one, it's the last one in the cycle. Three to the power of twenty is exactly five cycles, so it ends in one, the last digit of the cycle.
at: Three to the power of twenty

slides.say: Let's see one more example, two to the power of ten. Two, four, eight, sixteen, thirty-two. The last digits are two, four, eight, six, and then two again. Ten is eight plus two, so it's the second digit, four. And really, two to the power of ten is one thousand twenty-four.
at: Two to the power of ten

slides: Days, last digits, and the flags in a coming question all use the same tool. We divide by the length of the cycle, and look at the remainder. Let's see patterns in real questions. [pause] I'll see you in the next video.
